subject: Private inference headroom and scaling plan
messages:
From: Sam Jordan <sam.jordan@atlas-robotics.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Atlas Robotics SRE <eng@atlas-robotics.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kickoff - Private inference sizing (initial targets)

Hi Rishi —

Thanks for the intro call earlier. As promised, I'm sharing our target envelope so your team can propose sizing and an operational headroom plan for our on-prem VPC deployment. High-level:
- Peak concurrent requests: ~5k active sessions per minute during factory rush windows (10–12 mins bursts, 3x per day).
- Typical request profile: multimodal text+small imagery; median context length 512 tokens; p95 length 2048 tokens.
- P70 latency goal: <=150ms per token generated for interactive assistants; tail can be higher but must be <500ms per token ideally.
- Availability requirement: 99.95% monthly SLA; need clear fallbacks during capacity shortage.

Constraints:
- Rack-level networking limited to 25Gbps per top-of-rack uplink (current datacenter).
- We prefer to avoid shared public egress for model weights; want private peering to Redwood management plane.

Can you provide a recommended GPU mix, initial pool size, scaling algorithm (reactive vs scheduled), and a short failure-mode plan? Also list any data transfer or firewall rules we'll need.

Attached: our internal traffic snapshot (redacted).

Thanks — looking forward.

Sam
Head of Platform, Atlas Robotics
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Jordan <sam.jordan@atlas-robotics.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff - Private inference sizing (initial targets)

Sam —

Appreciate the detail. We've sketched an initial headroom model and a short-run scaling plan; attaching the workbook and a topology draft. High-level recommendations below, followed by open questions.

Summary recommendation (initial deployment):
- GPU mix: 8 x H100 80GB nodes (primary pool) + 2 x A100 80GB nodes (fallback/cheaper throughput for non-latency-critical batch jobs).
- Expected sustained throughput: ~4.2k concurrent sessions at median token length with per-token latency ~120–160ms (depending on batching).
- Headroom target: capacity to sustain 1.4x peak (plan for 7k concurrent-equivalent sessions) for at least 15 minutes to cover bursts.
- Autoscaling: hybrid model — scheduled warm pools for factory windows + reactive scale-out triggered by 85% token-processing utilization and rising queue length. Use conservative cooldown (180s) to prevent oscillation.
- Caching: deploy prefix/KV cache on the H100 nodes with an LRU eviction tuned to average 30% reuse to reduce compute by ~18% on conversational flows.

Network/infra notes:
- Top-of-rack 25Gbps is the hard constraint; for 8x H100 we estimate peak model weight fetch and KV replication will consume ~6–8Gbps; cross-host KV sync + shard traffic could reach 10Gbps during bursts. We’ll recommend dedicating a VLAN for inferencing traffic and enabling jumbo frames.
- Control plane peering: we'll use a private VPC peering with mutual TLS to the Redwood private control plane; this requires outbound TCP 443 to our management IPs and a static route on your side.

Fallbacks and graceful degradation:
1) Warm-down to a smaller, quantized model variant (A100 pool) when latency SLOs cannot be met, with a quality disclaimer returned via structured metadata.
2) Per-customer rate-limiting (on Atlas side) enforced at the edge with 429s and an informative retry-after header.
3) Opportunistic batching window extension during non-interactive bursts (for background jobs) to improve throughput.

Open questions we need from Atlas to finalize sizing:
- Typical token/sec generation rate per session (avg tokens generated per second) — you gave lengths but not generation rate.
- Acceptable percent of requests that can be downgraded to a smaller model variant during peak.
- Any regulatory requirements preventing model quantization or caching on customer premises.

Action items:
- Rishi: share headroom_modeling_v2.xlsx and topology SVG (attached) — DONE.
- Vivek: estimate network egress headroom and recommend NIC tuning — @Vivek, pls review below.
- Marissa: prepare draft SLA matrix and implications for committed capacity pricing.

If that looks good I’ll schedule a 45-min follow-up to walk the workbook with your SREs.

Cheers,
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Solutions Architecture
Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>, Sam Jordan <sam.jordan@atlas-robotics.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff - Private inference sizing (initial targets)

Rishi / Sam —

Quick network and perf addendum after running the headroom workbook against Atlas packet profiles. TL;DR: rack uplink is the most binding constraint for burst headroom; we need clear egress shaping and NIC-level interrupts tuned. Details: 

1) Throughput math (peak burst window assumptions):
- 5k sessions active, avg outgoing tokens/sec per session = 8 tokens/sec => 40k tokens/sec total.
- If avg token payload (post-encoding) is ~120 bytes, payload = ~4.8MB/s -> ~38.4Mbps (this seems low; note generation responses are bursty and per-token network amplification occurs with multi-chunk streaming).
- Real bottleneck is cross-host KV and model shard RPCs: during large contexts (p95 2048) KV sync increases and can add ~12–14Gbps internal traffic for the 8-node H100 cluster for a 12-minute burst.

2) NIC tuning & OS knobs:
- Enable RSS and adjust RPS/RFS to distribute interrupts across CPU cores tied to the inference process.
- Set MTU to 9000 where supported; reduces CPU per-packet overhead.
- Turn off flow-control on datacenter top-of-rack if possible and rely on priority flow control only for storage networks.

3) Autoscaling guidance:
- Scale-out threshold: when average token-processing utilization (kernel-level metric) >85% for 45s AND queue depth >250.
- Scale-in: only after target utilization <60% for 5 minutes and queue depth <50. 

4) Observability hooks needed from Atlas side:
- Expose token-level ingress counters, per-host KV hit ratio, NIC err/drop rates to our tracer.

5) Failure scenarios:
- If the 25Gbps uplink saturates, priority traffic (interactive tokens) should be allowed while background batching gets deprioritized and queued. Implement strict QoS markings on the switch.

Attaching a short NIC tuning checklist and a network topology draft that maps the 8 H100 nodes across two racks to avoid single-rack uplink saturation.

-Vivek
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>, Sam Jordan <sam.jordan@atlas-robotics.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 17:49:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff - Private inference sizing (initial targets)

Thanks team — this is shaping up well. Commercial notes and SLA implications: 

1) SLA sizing & committed capacity: to meet 99.95% with the headroom above we should propose a 12-month reserved pool (8 H100 + 2 A100) with a 20% overcommit credit line for burst capacity billed monthly if used. That gets us predictable throughput and a pricing lever for Atlas.

2) Credits & trial: offer a 30-day pilot with reduced commit (50% of proposed reserved capacity) and a one-time onboarding credit to cover tuning. Use pilot to validate KV hit ratio assumptions.

3) Contractual fallback language: include a clause that allows Redwood to automatically failover to a quantized variant when network saturation or GPU contention would otherwise breach the SLA; provide a customer-visible quality flag and a reduction in the monthly invoice if fallback is triggered >2% of billable minutes.

4) Next steps:
- Sam: confirm whether Atlas legal accepts the fallback language and whether they need pre-approved vendor images for on-prem agents.
- Rishi/Vivek/Dev: finalize runbook and NIC checklist; target to deliver a handoff-ready package by 2027-06-30.
- Marissa: I will draft the SLA matrix and commercial term sheet and share by Friday.

—Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success & GTM
Redwood Inference
